```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(lubridate)
source("utility-functions.R")

publications <- read_csv("../publications.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(date = paste(publication_date_year, publication_date_month,
                      publication_date_day, sep = '-')) %>%
  mutate(year = publication_date_year) %>%
  filter(include_in_full_cv == 'y') %>%
  arrange(-publication_date_year, -publication_date_month, -publication_date_day)

cv_entries <- read_csv("../cv_entries.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(include_in_full_cv == 'y') %>%
  mutate(date_start = paste(date_start_year, date_start_month,
                            date_start_day, sep = '-')) %>%
  mutate(date_end = paste(date_end_year, date_end_month,
                          date_end_day, sep = '-')) %>%
  mutate(year_begin = date_start_year) %>%
  mutate(year_end = date_end_year) %>%
  mutate(year = ifelse(is.na(year_end) | year_begin == year_end,
                       year_begin, str_c(year_begin, "–", year_end))) %>%
  mutate(across(2:4, as.numeric)) %>%
  arrange(-date_start_year, -date_start_month, -date_start_day)
```

## Research profile {.nohead .set-width-range}
```{block type="grid-item", echo=TRUE}
Computational evolutionary biologist working at the intersection of comparative genomics, evolutionary biology, and data science. My research investigates how genes with unknown function ("dark genes") originate, diversify, and acquire biological roles. I combine comparative genomics, phylogenomic analysis, sequence- and structure-based homology detection, and multi-omics approaches to investigate gene-family evolution and prioritize functional hypotheses across diverse biological systems.

My research spans coral, algal, amoebal, bacterial, and environmental microbial systems. I develop and apply computational workflows and analytical tools that address general problems in genomic discovery, from phylogenetic classification and genome annotation to metagenomic analysis and network-based interpretation. I have led collaborative computational research, mentored graduate and undergraduate researchers, and co-founded OceanOmics, translating biological research into environmental diagnostic technologies.
```

## Research areas {.nohead .set-width-range}
```{block type="grid-item", echo=TRUE}
- Evolutionary genomics and gene-family evolution
- Comparative genomics, phylogenomics, and phylogenetic methods
- Origins and evolution of novel and poorly characterized genes
- Genome annotation and computational protein characterization
- Metagenomics, multi-omics, and environmental genomics
- Reproducible bioinformatics workflows and research software
```

## Computational expertise and methods {.nohead .set-width-range}
```{block type="grid-item", echo=TRUE}
**Programming and research software:** *R* package development and maintenance; Python; Perl; shell-based bioinformatics scripting; reproducible analysis and version-controlled code.

**Comparative and evolutionary genomics:** phylogenetic and phylogenomic analysis; phylogenetic-tree screening and classification; gene-family comparison; genome annotation; sequence-based homology searches; comparative analysis of divergent genes.

**Metagenomics and multi-omics:** Snakemake-based workflow development; metagenomic quality control, assembly, binning, gene prediction, functional annotation, and quantification; integration of transcriptomic, proteomic, and genomic evidence.

**Network analysis and data structures:** graph-based network analysis using Python graph-tool; connected-component extraction, graph annotation, and network visualization.

**Computational infrastructure:** Linux/HPC environments; Conda/Mamba environments; SLURM-oriented workflow execution; Snakemake; Docker, Singularity, and Podman containerization.
```

## Research software and computational tools {.nohead .set-width-range}
```{block type="grid-item", echo=TRUE}
**PhySortR** — Creator and maintainer of the *R* port of a package for screening and sorting large collections of phylogenetic trees, identifying exclusive and non-exclusive clades in traditional and extended Newick formats. Available through CRAN (version 1.0.9; package DOI: [10.32614/CRAN.package.PhySortR](https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.PhySortR)). Original method described in Stephens et al., *PeerJ* (2016).

**Dinoflagellate Annotation Workflow** — Developed a workflow for protein-coding gene prediction in dinoflagellate genomes, integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, and *ab initio* gene-prediction evidence. Includes adaptations for non-standard dinoflagellate splice-site biology. [Source code](https://github.com/TimothyStephens/Dinoflagellate_Annotation_Workflow).

**naive ATLAS** — Adapted and extended the ATLAS metagenomic workflow to support recovery and analysis of microbial genomes across prokaryotes, microbial eukaryotes, viruses, and plasmids. Workflow includes quality control, assembly, binning, gene prediction, annotation, and quantification. [Source code](https://github.com/TimothyStephens/naive_atlas).

**Network Analysis Scripts** — Python utilities using *graph-tool* for graph construction, connected-component extraction, annotation, layout calculation, and visualization. [Source code](https://github.com/TimothyStephens/Network_Analysis_Scripts).

**MAGS-CodeDev** — Multi-agent graph-based software-development system that decomposes code projects into dependency graphs and coordinates code generation, testing, diagnosis, review, and iteration in isolated worktrees and containers. [Source code](https://github.com/TimothyStephens/MAGS-CodeDev).

**AgentBox** — Rootless Podman-based sandbox for running coding agents in project-scoped environments with explicit filesystem and network permissions. A software-infrastructure project demonstrating work in reproducible and constrained computational environments. [Source code](https://github.com/TimothyStephens/AgentBox).
```

## Research leadership and selected projects {.nohead .set-width-range}
```{block type="grid-item", echo=TRUE}
**Evolutionary origins of coral dark genes — NSF EDGE project**  
*Senior personnel; computational analysis and manuscript leadership.* Led computational analyses investigating the evolutionary origins of conserved dark-gene families in stony corals and contributed to the project's first research paper. The work found that approximately 82% of conserved coral dark-gene families were consistent with previously undetected homology to characterized gene families.  
[Related publication: Stephens et al., Genome Biology and Evolution (2026).]

**Computational enzyme discovery in Sargassum-associated microbial communities — Schmidt Sciences project**  
*Senior personnel; computational discovery.* Led computational discovery and prioritization of candidate enzyme families from microbial communities associated with *Sargassum* degradation, connecting comparative genomics with potential biomass-conversion applications.  
[Related publication: Nandi et al., Applied and Environmental Microbiology (2026).]

**Interdisciplinary environmental diagnostic development — OceanOmics**  
*Co-founder; scientific/technical leadership.* Led or coordinated interdisciplinary teams spanning biology, computer science, engineering, and synthetic biology in the development of environmental diagnostic platforms. Contributed to project development, technical problem-solving, funding acquisition, and progression of platforms toward proof of concept.
```

## Research mentoring and supervision {.nohead .set-width-range}
```{block type="grid-item", echo=TRUE}
Served as a day-to-day research mentor to nine graduate students and five undergraduate researchers in computational biology, genomics, and related areas.

**Graduate mentorship**

- Mentored three PhD students through completion.
- Each completed PhD mentee produced three to four first-author research papers during doctoral training.
- One former mentee is now an Assistant Professor.

**Student-led research**

- Oversaw 16 student-led research papers.
- Twelve of these papers included me as a co-first or second author.

Mentoring included research-question development, computational study design, analytical troubleshooting, interpretation, reproducibility, manuscript preparation, and knowledge transfer.
```

## Publications {.nohead .set-width-year}
```{r}
publications %>%
  mutate(ref2print = str_c(authors_full, " ", title, ". *", journal, "*")) %>%
  mutate(ref2print = ifelse(!is.na(ref_info),
                            str_c(ref2print, ", ", ref_info, ", ", year(date), "."),
                            str_c(ref2print, ", ", year(date), "."))) %>%
  mutate(ref2print = ifelse(!is.na(preprint),
                            str_c(ref2print, " [[Preprint](", preprint, ")]"),
                            ref2print)) %>%
  mutate(ref2print = ifelse(!is.na(url),
                            str_c(ref2print, " [[DOI/URL](", url, ")]"),
                            ref2print)) %>%
  mutate(ref2print = ifelse(!is.na(pdf),
                            str_c(ref2print, " [[PDF](", pdf, ")]"),
                            ref2print)) %>%
  mutate(ref2print = ifelse(!is.na(additional_info),
                            str_c(ref2print, " ", additional_info),
                            ref2print)) %>%
  select(year, ref2print) %>%
  #manual_page_break_after_row("ref2print", "PhySortR: a fast, flexible tool for sorting phylogenetic trees in R") %>%
  knitr::kable()
```
